topic: What interference mitigation techniques are viable for overlapping service transmissions across geographically dispersed ground stations?
response: For overlapping service transmissions across geographically dispersed ground stations, viable interference mitigation techniques include Rate-Splitting Multiple Access (RSMA) and Analog Beamforming. RSMA can provide high throughput while mitigating co-channel interference by splitting the available bandwidth among multiple groups of users. Analog Beamforming can reduce interference by directing the transmitted signal towards specific areas, reducing overlap with other signals.
reference_context: The context references various studies on interference mitigation in satellite and terrestrial networks, including RSMA for multigroup multicast and multibeam satellite systems, and analog beamforming for spectrum sharing backhaul satellite-terrestrial systems.
